question: An equilateral triangle of side 6 cm has its corners cut-off to form a regular hexagon. What is the area of this regular hexagon?
solution:
**Given:**

Side of the equilateral triangle = 6 cm

**Concept:**

Area of the regular hexagon = 6 × √3/4 (side)² 

**Solution:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/17a7108a141637e210821ffb05e06fd46b5d45b13ffe88fa3ae25aae5a2a95a6.png] 

In the above-shown figure, 

Equilateral Δ ABC, its corners cut-off to form a regular hexagon

From the figure, we can say that, 

a + a + a = 6

⇒ 3a = 6

⇒ a = 2

Side of hexagon, PQRSTU = a = 2 cm

Area of a hexagon = 6 × √3/4 (side)2 

⇒ Area = 6 × √3/4 (2)2 

⇒ Area = 6 × √3/4 × 4

⇒ Area = 6√3 cm²

**Therefore, the area of this regular hexagon is ** **6√3 cm².**
